nodes.label: Upload coordinator
nodes.rationale: The coordinator owns routing, workflow state, and the single selected location while provider adapters own bytes and provider metadata.

nodes.label: Provider adapter boundary
nodes.rationale: Provider-specific HTTP, OAuth, signing, and error normalization stay behind capability-neutral ports so the service owns policy and tenant checks.

nodes.label: Configuration boundary architecture
nodes.rationale: The later design deliberately removes every secret-adjacent field from committed JSON and makes code-level environment names the single convention.

nodes.label: Single-location database model
nodes.rationale: Database constraints bind each ready logical object to exactly one verified provider location and reject replica-style schema designs.

nodes.label: Direct-to-provider transfer
nodes.rationale: The original common chunk interface was rejected because it implied proxying; Drive sessions and fallback capabilities are intentionally different direct transfer mechanisms.

nodes.label: Same-provider reconciliation
nodes.rationale: Ambiguous results are inspected on the selected provider and may not trigger content writes to another provider.

nodes.label: Leased background job queue
nodes.rationale: Jobs use conditional leases with ownership checks; expiry makes work claimable again but does not authorize a replacement remote mutation.

nodes.label: Operator routing controls
nodes.rationale: Fault injection and forced fallback answer different operational questions and remain subordinate to authorization, mutation, consent, and configuration gates.

nodes.label: Explicit Drive folder recovery
nodes.rationale: The app-managed folder is created or found at connection setup, but deletion or duplicate names require explicit recovery rather than silent replacement or fallback.
